# Running init, and what it installs

Purpose: the exact `toolkit init` commands, what init writes and in what
order, what to do when it stops, and which files each setup answer installs.

## Contents

- The init command
- What init does, in order
- A failed or stopped run
- Running init inside Codex
- What init installs
- How the answers shape the files

## The init command

Run one of these alone, with the owner's answers. One-line values go in
single quotes; write an apostrophe inside them as `'\''`.

```text
toolkit init --name '<name>' --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner '<owner>' --backup-dir '<folder>'
toolkit init --name '<name>' --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner '<owner>' --backup-dir '<folder>' --salesforce
```

- `--tracker`: `local`, `notion`, `github`, or `jira`.
- `--memory`: `builtin`, `hindsight`, or `notion`.
- `--backup-dir`: the folder from question 6, or `none`. Leave it out only
  with a Notion tracker and Notion memory: Notion keeps each page's history
  and keeps deleted pages in its trash, so no folder is asked for.
- Add `--decline SOUL.md` after a no to question 5.
- `--hosts` defaults to both hosts (`claude-code,codex`). Leave it out unless
  the owner uses only one.

Example:

```text
toolkit init --name 'Acme CRM' --key acme-crm --tracker local --memory builtin --owner 'Mike Rihm' --backup-dir '~/Backups/toolkit' --decline SOUL.md
```

Then record what init has no flag for:

```text
toolkit config set tracker.idPrefix <prefix>
toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.sandbox <alias>
toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.production <alias>
```

The id prefix can change only before the first work item exists. The backup
folder changes later with `toolkit config set backup.dir <folder>` (or
`none`).

## What init does, in order

1. Works out the settings from the flags.
2. Plans every file. A setup marker error stops here, before any write.
3. Hindsight memory: checks that the local server answers. Nothing is written
   yet.
4. Wires the backends: builds the Notion pages and databases
   (`toolkit notion ensure-project`) and the Hindsight bank
   (`toolkit hindsight ensure-bank`) when chosen.
5. Writes the files: in Codex's own folders (`.codex/`, `.agents/`) first,
   then the rest.
6. Builds `.work-items/DASHBOARD.md` and `.memory/MEMORY.md`.
7. Writes `.toolkit.json`, last.

So a Notion or Hindsight project needs its backend ready before init runs:
`wiring-notion.md` and `wiring-hindsight.md` in this folder.

## A failed or stopped run

- Every run is safe to repeat. `.toolkit.json` is written last, and a second
  run reuses the Notion and Hindsight ids an earlier run made.
- Read the message and its fix line. Fix the cause, then run the same command
  again.
- Never change an answer the owner gave (hosts, tracker, memory, Salesforce,
  `SOUL.md`) to get past an error. Never set the project up in another folder
  and copy it over. Stop, say what failed, and say what he must approve or
  run.

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| No Notion root page is known on this computer | `wiring-notion.md`, "Before init" |
| The local Hindsight server does not answer | `wiring-hindsight.md`, "Before init" |
| Could not write `.codex/` (or `.agents/`) | "Running init inside Codex", below |
| The Codex sandbox blocked init's request to Hindsight | "Running init inside Codex", below |
| With Notion, init reports another id prefix, because `WI` is used there | Say the prefix it took in one line |

## Running init inside Codex

Init writes `.codex/` and `.agents/` first, and the Codex sandbox refuses
both. Its request to the local Hindsight server is also blocked there.

1. Before running it, tell the owner that Codex will ask to run init outside
   the sandbox.
2. Run init alone, with `sandbox_permissions` set to `require_escalated` and a
   one-line reason ("Set up Toolkit V2 in this project: write .codex/,
   .agents/, and the project files.").
3. It stops with "Could not write ... .codex/" (or `.agents/`), or says the
   Codex sandbox blocked its request to Hindsight: nothing else was written.
   Show the owner the exact command init printed, and ask him to approve it
   or to run it in a terminal.

A brand-new folder in Codex: Codex lists `project-setup` in every folder once
`toolkit machine-setup` has turned the toolkit plugin on for every folder. The
other Toolkit V2 skills appear only after init, in a new session.

## What init installs

The toolkit plugin carries an exact copy of the model project in its
`scaffold/model/` folder. Init copies it and applies the answers.

| Installed | When |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT.md`, `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore` | Every project |
| `SOUL.md` | Every project, unless the owner declined it |
| `requirements/` (its own `AGENTS.md`, `SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md`, and `system-area-template/`), `system-guide/AREA-TEMPLATE.md`, `tests/TEST-PLAN-TEMPLATE.md`, `ai-external-knowledge/INDEX.md` | Every project |
| The general rules in `.claude/rules/` | Every project (Codex reads them through `AGENTS.md`) |
| A root `CLAUDE.md` holding only `@AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/output-styles/plain-english.md` | Claude Code is one of the hosts |
| `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/rules/toolkit.rules` (written by the toolkit; the model has neither) | Codex is one of the hosts |
| `.work-items/work-item-template/` (`WORK-ITEM.md`, `DESIGN.md`) and `.claude/rules/work-item-folders.md` | Local folders tracker |
| `.memory/` seed files: `AGENTS.md`, `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `memory-criteria.md`, `project_topic_template.md`, `terminology-glossary.md` | Built-in memory |
| `delivery/`, `sfdx-project.json`, `.forceignore`, `tools/kb/`, `tools/permissions/`, the two guard hooks in `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/protected-orgs.json`, and the Salesforce rules | Salesforce projects |
| The `sf-*` skills in `.claude/skills/` | Salesforce projects with Claude Code as a host |
| `.codex/hooks.json` (runs the two guard hooks in Codex) and the `sf-*` skills in `.agents/skills/` | Salesforce projects with Codex as a host |

It also turns the Toolkit V2 plugins on for this project, and every
`*@claude-toolkit` plugin off here. It never copies work items or memory
records, and never copies the model's `.vscode/` or `.sfdx/` folders.

## How the answers shape the files

- `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and `PROJECT.md` carry setup markers such as
  `<!-- if tracker=local -->` ... `<!-- endif -->`. Init keeps the lines for
  the answers given and removes the rest, markers included.
- The rules list in `AGENTS.md`, between `<!-- toolkit:rules:start -->` and
  `<!-- toolkit:rules:end -->`, is written from the files in `.claude/rules/`
  and rebuilt on every `toolkit sync`. Never edit it by hand.
- A project that is not a Salesforce project gets no Salesforce hooks or `sf`
  permission lines in `.claude/settings.json`, and no Salesforce lines in
  `.gitignore`.
- `.memory/MEMORY.md` is generated: init installs the model's copy, then
  `toolkit memory reindex` rebuilds it.
- A file the project already has is kept. `.gitignore`, the settings, and the
  Codex files get the toolkit's lines merged in.
- Instruction files follow the model: `AGENTS.md` holds the instructions, and
  one root `CLAUDE.md` holds only `@AGENTS.md`. There is no other
  `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or `CLAUDE.local.md`. Doctor checks this.
  Because the root `CLAUDE.md` exists, Claude Code does not load a
  subfolder's `AGENTS.md` by itself; the root `AGENTS.md` tells the agent to
  read it before editing in that folder. Ask before changing or removing a
  `CLAUDE.md` the owner wrote.

# Finishing setup

Purpose: after init and wiring, fill the setup guides with confirmed facts,
set up backups, get doctor to 0 problems, record the owner's steps, and end
with the report and the commit offer.

## Contents

- Filling the setup guides
- SOUL.md
- Backups
- Doctor
- The owner's steps and the current focus
- The report
- The commit offer

## Filling the setup guides

The copied files start with a fill-in guide comment and hold
`<angle bracket>` prompts. Init fills the project name. The rest is filled only with
facts the owner confirmed, in this order:

1. **The project's outcome** in `AGENTS.md`. It is the owner's answer, never a
   sentence worked out from the code, the tests, or the README. Ask it as its
   own question, with a suggestion from the repository:

   > What should this project do for you, in one sentence? From the code I'd suggest: "Export invoices to the bank's CSV format every Friday."

   Until he answers, leave the outcome prompts in `AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT.md`,
   and `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`, and list them in the report.
2. **The "Build, test, or deploy" row** under Commands in `AGENTS.md`. Ask,
   with a recommendation from what the repository shows (for example
   `npm test`).
3. **`PROJECT.md` and `README.md`.** Follow each file's guide. Ask only what
   the repository cannot answer.
4. **`PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`** (the outcome, phases, and work units) and
   **`requirements/SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md`** (accepted data model requirements):
   fill them only when the owner already knows the facts. On a new project
   they usually stay as they are and are listed as prompts left. The data
   model gets only accepted requirements, never a guess.
5. Delete each fill-in guide comment once its file is filled.

Never invent a fact to fill a prompt. Each prompt that is left goes in the
report, with the fact it needs.

## SOUL.md

- The owner said yes: fill it with his words and get his approval of the
  text.
- He said no before init: init had `--decline SOUL.md`, and the file was never
  installed.
- He turns it down after init: record the no, then delete the file, so sync
  never brings it back and doctor does not report it missing.

  ```text
  toolkit config set declined SOUL.md
  ```

  `toolkit config set declined none` undoes it.

## Backups

Init recorded the backup folder (`--backup-dir`). From now on
`toolkit work finish` and every handoff back up the parts that live only on
this computer, to `<backup folder>/<project key>-<YYYY-MM-DD>/`.

1. Make the first backup now, so a folder that cannot be reached (for
   example an external drive that is not connected) shows up during setup:

   ```text
   toolkit handoff-backup
   ```

2. It prints one line saying what it copied. A failure line goes in the
   report, with its fix.
3. The owner chose no folder (`none`), or init ran without one: say in the
   report that nothing is backed up, and that doctor will keep noting it.
4. Tracker and memory both in Notion: there is no folder and no first
   backup. Say in the report, in one line, that Notion keeps each page's
   history and keeps deleted pages in its trash, so no backup folder is
   needed. Doctor gives no backup warning for this project.

What each backup holds, and restoring: `backup-and-restore.md` in this
folder.

## Doctor

Run doctor until it reports 0 problems:

```text
toolkit doctor
```

- Fix each problem with the fix doctor names, then run it again.
- A warning only the other host can clear (for example Codex hook trust, seen
  from Claude Code) is the owner's step. It does not block setup, and it does
  not make doctor fail when run from Claude Code.

## The owner's steps and the current focus

Setup is not a work item. Never create one for setup steps, and never add
made-up owner questions to finish setup.

| Owner step | In the reply | In the current focus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ntn login` (Notion, when `ntn whoami` fails) | Yes | Yes, under "Waiting on the owner" |
| Trust this project folder in Codex (Codex asks when it opens the folder) | Yes | Yes, under "Waiting on the owner" |
| Trust the hooks in Codex (`/hooks`) | Yes | Yes, under "Waiting on the owner" |
| Approve Codex running init outside its sandbox | Yes | No |
| Start a new session | Yes | No |

A focus line for a step doctor checks is marked so a later session knows when
to drop it:

```markdown
- Trust this folder in Codex: open Codex here and trust the folder when it asks. Setup step; drop it when doctor stops reporting it.
- Trust the Toolkit V2 hooks in Codex: open Codex here, type /hooks, trust them. Setup step; drop it when doctor stops reporting it.
```

Save the focus. The format, the version check, and the fill-in guide on a new
project: `current-focus.md` in this folder. Read it with its version, change
it, and save the whole text with that version. Keep the `# Current focus`
title and set the "Last updated" line, for example
`Last updated: 2026-09-28, setup, agent`. Run only the save for this host.

```text
toolkit memory focus --json
toolkit memory focus --set-file - --expect <version>
toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
```

The first save is Claude Code, with the text in a quoted heredoc (the
command, the text, then a line holding only `EOF`). The second is Codex.

Then show the first briefing:

```text
toolkit brief
```

## The report

A short plain report, in this order:

1. What was set up, as a short list the owner can check: tracker, memory,
   Salesforce or not, the files added.
2. What was skipped, and why.
3. What the owner must do himself, each with why.
4. Doctor's result: 0 problems, or each remaining problem with its fix.
5. The prompts left, each with the fact it needs.
6. The last line: the commit offer.

## The commit offer

The setup files are not committed yet, and the first merge of a work item
needs them committed. The reply's last line is:

> Setup files are not committed. Commit them now?

After a yes:

- Stage the files init wrote, each by name. Never `git add -A` or
  `git add .`.
- Read the staged list. No `.work-items/` or `.memory/` file may be in it.
- `git diff --cached --check` lists template lines that end with two spaces.
  They are Markdown line breaks from the model's templates: leave them, and
  commit the files as init wrote them.
- Commit with a plain message and no AI credit (for example
  `git commit -m 'Set up Toolkit V2'`).
- Codex: each Git command alone, with escalated permissions, or run by the
  owner in a terminal when Codex refuses it without asking.

The full rules: `git-rules.md` in this folder. After the commit, the reply's
last line is "Tell me the first thing you want built."

# The current focus

Purpose: the format of the current focus, when to change it, and the exact
read-change-save sequence, in every memory backend.

## Contents

- What the focus is for
- The format
- What goes in each section
- When to check it
- Read, change, save
- A new project's focus
- Examples
- Checklist for a focus save

## What the focus is for

The current focus is the first thing the next session reads: the session
briefing includes it. It says what is happening now and where the next
session starts. It never repeats the tracker: a work item's status, tasks,
and history stay in the work item.

| Backend | Where the focus lives |
| --- | --- |
| Built-in | `.memory/CURRENT_FOCUS.md` in the main checkout |
| Hindsight | The document `focus` in the project's bank |
| Notion | The "Current focus" page under the project's page |

The same commands read and save it in every backend. Never edit the file or
the page by hand.

## The format

The model's format: a `# Current focus` title line, a `Last updated:` line,
then exactly four `##` sections in this order, under 50 lines in total.

```markdown
# Current focus

Last updated: <YYYY-MM-DD>, <source>, <person or agent>

## Now

## Waiting on the owner

## Untracked to-dos

## Next session starts with
```

What the command enforces:

- It refuses a focus that lacks one of the four sections, has another
  section, or is over 50 lines (exit code 2, nothing saved).
- It adds the title line or the `Last updated:` line when either is missing,
  and sets an older date to today. It cannot know the source or who wrote
  it, so write the line yourself.

## What goes in each section

- **Last updated:** the date, the source (for example `handoff`,
  `work-finish`, `chat`), and who wrote it (a person, or `agent`). Change it
  on every save.
- **Now:** the current outcome or area, with work item ids and titles only,
  for example `- WI-012 CSV export`. Never a status or a stage: the tracker
  holds those.
- **Waiting on the owner:** a decision or action only the owner can take
  that has no work item: what it is, who needs it, and when to check again.
  Work items that wait on him are listed by `toolkit work decisions`, not
  here. A setup step (trust the hooks in Codex, sign in to Notion with
  `ntn login`) stays only while `toolkit doctor` still reports it.
- **Untracked to-dos:** things the owner asked for that have no work item.
  When one becomes a work item, replace the line with the item's id under
  Now.
- **Next session starts with:** one entry: where to resume, what to read,
  and the next action. It is replaced at each handoff, not added to.
- Write "None." in a section with nothing in it.
- Keep it under 50 lines by replacing stale lines, never by appending. Never
  drop an owner to-do that is still open only to meet the limit.

## When to check it

Check the focus before the reply ends when:

- a work item's stage changes, or its next step changes to something the
  focus does not say. Check two things:
  1. Now lists the item (id and title). Add it when it is missing; take it
     off when the item is Done or Cancelled. For Done, take it off just
     before `toolkit work finish`, which backs up the focus as it is then.
  2. Next session starts with does not name a step that is done or no longer
     next. Replace that line with the item's real next step, in one line that
     points at the item, for example "Continue WI-012 from its Resume here:
     build P1."
- the owner asks for something with no work item (add it under Untracked
  to-dos), or a decision only he can make has no work item (Waiting on the
  owner).
- `toolkit doctor` no longer reports a setup step listed under Waiting on the
  owner (drop it).
- a session hands off (replace the one entry under Next session starts
  with).

Skip the save when nothing in the focus is wrong. Leave every line you are
not changing exactly as it is.

## Read, change, save

1. Read it with its version. The output has `text` and `version`:

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus --json
   ```

2. Change only the lines that need it, in the whole text, and update the
   `Last updated:` line.
3. Save the whole text with the version you read.
   Claude Code: `<file>` is `-`, with the text on standard input after a
   quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`), then a line holding only `EOF`.

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus --set-file <file> --expect <version>
   ```

   Codex: give the text in single quotes instead (newlines are kept), or
   use a file in a new `mktemp -d` folder and delete it after the save.
   Write an apostrophe as ’ (the curly apostrophe, U+2019), or reword the
   text. Never `'\''` in Codex: the project's command rule does not match
   that form, so the command runs inside the sandbox, and the tool call can
   drop the backslash.

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus --text '<text>' --expect <version>
   ```

4. Exit code 2 with "changed since it was read" means another session saved
   the focus after you read it. Read it again, make your change in the new
   text, and save with the new version. Never save without `--expect`: that
   would silently drop the other session's change.
5. No focus yet (`version` is null): save with `--expect absent`, in the full
   format above.
6. Read it back:

   ```text
   toolkit memory focus
   ```

## A new project's focus

A new project's focus still holds the model's setup text: a fill-in guide
comment under the title (`<!-- Fill-in guide: ... -->`) and an
`<angle-bracket>` prompt in every section. At the first save:

- remove the fill-in guide comment;
- replace each prompt with real content, or with "None." when there is none;
- never leave an angle-bracket prompt in a saved focus.

## Examples

A full focus:

```markdown
# Current focus

Last updated: 2026-09-26, handoff, agent

## Now

- WI-012 CSV export
- WI-015 Large exports (sub-item of WI-012)

## Waiting on the owner

- Pick a hosting provider before the first deploy (no work item yet); check again 2026-10-01.

## Untracked to-dos

- Email the client about the October demo.

## Next session starts with

- 2026-09-26 17:40 UTC | CSV export: continue WI-012 from its Resume here. Goal: exports finish under 10 seconds.
```

The handoff entry with a work item is a pointer only:
`<UTC date and time> | <topic>: continue <WI-id> from its Resume here. Goal: <one line>.`

With no work item, the entry is a short note: the goal or topic, where work
stopped, the first next action, limits on what may be done without the
owner, and open questions. Do not create a work item only to hold it.

## Checklist for a focus save

- [ ] Read with `--json`; you have the version.
- [ ] The `# Current focus` title and the `Last updated:` line (date,
      source, who) are there.
- [ ] Four sections, in order; "None." in each empty one.
- [ ] Work item ids and titles only; no status or stage.
- [ ] No angle-bracket prompt and no fill-in guide comment left.
- [ ] Under 50 lines; no open owner to-do dropped.
- [ ] Saved with `--expect`; read back.

# Git rules for Toolkit V2 skills

Purpose: the Git rules every Toolkit V2 skill follows when it makes a branch,
commits, merges, pushes, or removes a worktree, in Claude Code and in Codex.

## Contents

- Look before the first Git write
- Branch and worktree names for a work item
- Staging and committing
- No AI credit
- The Git-ignored toolkit folders
- A project with no remote
- The merge-safety check
- A merge that stops on a conflict
- Git writes in Codex
- Checklist: one commit
- Examples

## Look before the first Git write

Other sessions may work in the same repository at the same time. Before the
first Git write in a session, run each of these on its own:

```text
git worktree list
git status
git remote
```

- `git remote` prints nothing: the project has no remote. Read "A project
  with no remote" below before any fetch, pull, push, or pull request.
- An unknown worktree, a branch that moved, or a change this session did not
  make means another session is working. Do not change it. Tell the owner.
- The shared primary checkout is the first entry `git worktree list` prints.
  In it, never switch branches, reset, rebase, or stash.
- Never commit, push, rebase, or delete another session's branch, and never
  commit its uncommitted changes, even when they look finished.

## Branch and worktree names for a work item

A work item's code work happens in its own worktree, on its own branch.

| Part | Form | Example for `WI-007`, "CSV export" |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Branch | `claude/<prefix>-<number>-<slug>` | `claude/wi-007-csv-export` |
| Worktree folder | `.claude/worktrees/<prefix>-<number>-<slug>` | `.claude/worktrees/wi-007-csv-export` |

- `<prefix>` is the item's own id prefix in lower case: `wi` for `WI-007`,
  `tv2` for `TV2-007`, `acme` for `ACME-007`.
- The session briefing and `merge-and-clean-up` find the item from the id in
  the branch name. A branch named `wi-001-<slug>` for item `TV2-001` is not
  linked to that item.
- Make both with one command:

  ```text
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/wi-007-csv-export -b claude/wi-007-csv-export
  ```

- Build on the item's branch, never on the default branch.

## Staging and committing

- Stage each path by name. Never run `git add -A`, `git add .`, or
  `git commit -a`: in a shared checkout they take other sessions' files.
- Read the staged file list, then the full staged diff, before the commit.
  Unstage any file this session did not write.

  ```text
  git diff --cached --name-status
  git diff --cached
  ```

- Write a plain commit message that says what changed, in one line when one
  line is enough.

## No AI credit

Nothing committed or published names an AI as an author or a helper:

- no `Co-Authored-By:` line naming an AI (a line naming a real person is
  allowed);
- no "Generated with" line;
- no AI credit in a pull request title or description, a code comment, a file
  header, or release notes.

The pre-tool hook refuses a commit or pull request command that carries such
a line. When it refuses, change the wording. Never commit another way to get
past it.

## The Git-ignored toolkit folders

`.work-items/` and `.memory/` are Git-ignored and live in the main checkout.

- Never commit them, and never force them in with `git add -f`. The hook
  refuses it.
- Never run `git clean -x` or `git clean -X` in the main checkout. It deletes
  both folders, and Git cannot bring them back. The hook refuses it.
- They change only through `toolkit work` and `toolkit memory` commands.
- Their backup is automatic: `toolkit work finish` and the handoff copy them
  to the owner's backup folder (`toolkit handoff-backup` does the same on
  request). `toolkit export --to <folder>` makes a one-off copy.

## A project with no remote

`git remote` prints nothing.

- Never run `git fetch`, `git pull`, or `git push`. A fetch that fails or is
  refused is not a blocker: never report it as one, and never write it into a
  work item.
- There is no pull request. `work-finish` merges the item's branch into the
  default branch locally, after the same approval a pull request merge needs,
  from the main checkout:

  ```text
  git merge --ff-only claude/wi-007-csv-export
  ```

  Then it adds the history note "No remote: merged locally into
  <default branch>."
- The fast-forward fails when the default branch moved on after the item's
  branch was made (for example another item's local merge). Merge the default
  branch into the item's branch in the item's worktree (`git merge main`, with
  the real default branch name), run the item's checks again, then run the
  fast-forward again.
- Documents are committed on the local default branch. `publish-docs` does
  this by itself.
- `merge-and-clean-up`, `pull-latest`, and `reset-to-remote` have nothing to
  do. Say so in one line.

## The merge-safety check

Before any merge into the default branch, check that it cannot overwrite
another session's uncommitted work in the primary checkout. With a remote,
fetch first so the comparison uses the remote's default branch.

```text
git diff --name-only main...claude/wi-007-csv-export
git -C <primary checkout> status --porcelain
```

Use the real default branch name, and `origin/<default branch>` when there is
a remote. A file in both lists: stop, name exactly those files, and let the
owner decide whether to commit, stash, or wait. Never touch the primary
checkout's changes yourself.

## A merge that stops on a conflict

1. Read both sides of each conflicting file. When the right result is not
   clear from the two sides, stop and ask the owner.
2. Stage each resolved file by name.
3. Commit with a message you write:

   ```text
   git commit -m 'Merge main into claude/wi-007-csv-export: keep both export formats'
   ```

Never run `git commit --no-edit` after a conflict: it keeps Git's
"# Conflicts:" lines in the message.

## Git writes in Codex

Codex's sandbox keeps `.git/` read-only. Every command that writes `.git/`
fails inside it: `git add`, `commit`, `merge`, `fetch`, `pull`, `push`,
`switch`, `checkout`, `restore`, `rm`, `mv`, `stash`, `cherry-pick`,
`revert`, `rebase`, `reset`, `update-ref`, `git worktree add`, `remove`,
`move`, `prune`, and `repair`, and `git branch -d`, `-D`, `-m`, `-c`, and
`-f`. The project's
`.codex/rules/toolkit.rules` makes Codex ask the owner before each one. A `gh`
call that needs the network is also refused inside the sandbox.

Reading commands (`git status`, `git log`, `git diff`, `git show`,
`git branch --list`, `git worktree list`) run inside the sandbox as usual.

For each Git write in Codex:

- [ ] Run the Git command alone, as its own command: not joined to another
      command with `&&`, `;`, or a pipe, and not from a script.
- [ ] Say in one line what the command does, before Codex asks the owner.
- [ ] Ask for escalated permissions: set `sandbox_permissions` to
      `require_escalated`, with a one-line reason that says what the command
      does ("Create the worktree for WI-002 on its own branch."). An approval
      without escalation still runs the command inside the sandbox, where it
      fails on `.git/index.lock`.
- [ ] Codex refused it without asking ("approval required by policy", or
      "AskForApproval is set to Never"): this session cannot ask. Stop that
      step, show the owner the exact command, and ask him to approve it in an
      interactive session or run it in a terminal. Set the work item waiting
      on the owner. It is not an outside blocker.

Never work around a refusal: no nested `git clone` of the project, no copy of
`.git/`, no script that runs Git for you, and no building on the default
branch instead of the item's branch. The `publish-docs` script is not such a
script: it is that skill's own tool. Run it alone with escalated permissions,
like any other Git write.

## Checklist: one commit

```text
- [ ] In the right worktree, on the right branch (git branch --show-current)
- [ ] Each path staged by name
- [ ] Staged list read: only this session's files, no .work-items/ or .memory/
- [ ] Full staged diff read
- [ ] Plain message with no AI credit line
- [ ] Codex: each Git command run alone, with escalated permissions
```

## Examples

Right: stage by name, read the list, commit.

```text
git add src/export.js tests/export.test.js
git diff --cached --name-status
git commit -m 'Add CSV export for invoices'
```

Wrong: `git add -A && git commit -m 'wip'`. It stages other sessions' files,
and in Codex the joined command runs inside the sandbox and fails.

Wrong: a message whose last line is a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming an AI
model. The hook refuses it. Remove the line and commit again.

Right, no remote: after the owner approves the result and the merge,

```text
git merge --ff-only claude/wi-007-csv-export
```

run from the main checkout, then the history note "No remote: merged locally
into main."

Right, Codex: `git commit -m 'Add CSV export for invoices'` run alone, with
`sandbox_permissions` set to `require_escalated` and the reason "Commit the
CSV export files for WI-007 on its branch."

Then replace the one-sentence outcome below and the "Build, test, or deploy" row under Commands with this project's confirmed values. Change paths only when the installed folder differs. <One sentence describing this project and its outcome.> The owner named in `PROJECT.md` makes this project's decisions. The agent runs the project: it keeps the work tracker, memory, and project records current, and it does the technical work.

## Every session

- The session-start hook adds a "Project briefing" to your context: this worktree's work item, active items with the skill that continues each one, what waits on the owner, the current focus, moved items, and setup warnings. If there is no briefing, run `toolkit brief` and read it.
- Read `SOUL.md` (when the project has one) and `PROJECT.md`; read them again after resume, clear, or compaction.
- Anything to build, add, fix, or change, and "keep going": the `work-on` skill. It opens the work item; also read the item's phase in `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`.
- A change to a requirement, such as R-01, at any stage: `work-requirements`.
- "You drive", "take it from here", "run with it", even about a named item: `work-delegate`.
- "Where are we": `work-status`. "What do you need from me" and approvals: `work-decide`.
- "Remember", "from now on", "always", "never", "forget that": `memory-save`. It puts an instruction for how the agent works in the rules and a fact in memory. "What did we decide": `memory-find`.
- Open the matching skill or rule when the task needs its procedure. Method skills from other plugins (brainstorming, plans, debugging) may run inside these skills, never instead of them.
- Before editing files in a folder that has its own `AGENTS.md` (for example `requirements/`), read that file.
- Codex: at session start, read the always-on rules listed under "Rules".

## What the owner decides

Ask the owner and record the answer before you:
- approve requirements (build and data-load work cannot pass stage `03` without it; requirements count as approved only when the item records the owner's approval with a date; a saved draft is not approved);
- choose or approve a design, approve a finished result, or mark work Done or Cancelled;
- merge to the default branch (unless `DECISIONS.md` records a standing merge instruction), deploy, or do anything that cannot be undone;
- spend money, sign in, or change an account.

Do everything else yourself, record it, and report it. When you need a decision, add it to the work item's Open Questions with "Decision needed from: owner" and set the item's `waiting_on` to `owner` ("Work tracking" says how).

## Where information goes

| Information | Home |
| --- | --- |
| New request, idea, or bug | A new work item at stage `01-discovery` (`work-on`) |
| Requirements, questions, tasks, progress, and history of one change | That work item |
| How a change is built | `DESIGN.md` beside the item's `WORK-ITEM.md` (`toolkit work design`) |
| A decision for the whole project | `DECISIONS.md` (`work-decide`) |
| Phases and deliverable-sized work units | `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`, naming each unit's work item ID |
| A work item's test plan | `tests/`, a copy of `TEST-PLAN-TEMPLATE.md` named for the item, committed on the item's branch; never in the tracker |
| Agreed behavior, after delivery | The area's file in `requirements/`, at stage `14-spec-update` |
| Verified structure of the current system | The area's file in `system-guide/` |
| What is in progress, owner to-dos with no work item, where the next session starts | The current focus (`memory-save`) |
| The owner's preference or correction for how the agent works ("from now on", "always", "never") | `.claude/rules/owner-preferences.md` (`memory-save` runs `toolkit rule add`); for every project, `~/.claude/rules/` |
| A lasting fact, an unproven lesson, or a hard-to-find reference | Memory (`memory-save`) |
| Project terms | The glossary (`memory-save`) |
| Outside documentation you capture | `ai-external-knowledge/`, one folder per topic |
| How agents should work in this project, or a procedure that proved itself | A rule in `.claude/rules/` or a skill in `.claude/skills/`, with the owner's yes; never memory |

Authorized edits to committed project documents are saved with `.claude/rules/publish-project-documents.md` and the `publish-docs` skill. Local work items and local memory are Git-ignored and never committed.

## Work tracking

- Tracker: local folders in `.work-items/`, Git-ignored, in the main checkout, shared by every worktree. `.claude/rules/work-item-folders.md` covers folders, moves, and generated files. A sub-item is an item folder nested inside its parent item's folder. It is the only tracker; never copy items into a second tracker or a local list.
- IDs look like `WI-001` (the prefix is `tracker.idPrefix` in `.toolkit.json`). Refer to work items by ID, never by folder path. The owner may move or rename item folders; find them by ID and continue. Change `waiting_on`, the stage, and other fields with `toolkit work` commands.
- Keep each design with its item after delivery. The roadmap names items by ID; item detail stays in the tracker.
- Stages `01-discovery` to `14-spec-update`, statuses, and approval gates: `toolkit work lifecycle`.

## Memory

- System: built-in memory in `.memory/`, Git-ignored, in the main checkout, shared by every worktree. It can be opened as an Obsidian vault. Read `.memory/AGENTS.md` before working there. What is worth saving: `.memory/memory-criteria.md`.
- Read and write memory only through the `memory-save`, `memory-find`, and `memory-tidy` skills, which run `toolkit memory` commands. Search memory before asking the owner to repeat something. When a save needs the owner's yes: the `memory-save` skill. Never store secrets, email addresses, or work-item status.

## Rules

The toolkit writes the list between the two markers from the files in `.claude/rules/` and rebuilds it on every `toolkit sync`. Do not edit it by hand.

<!-- toolkit:rules:start -->
Always on. Claude Code loads these at session start. Codex: read each one at session start.
- `.claude/rules/humanize-outbound-text.md`: Humanize Anything Sent to Another Person
- `.claude/rules/keep-work-item-current.md`: Keep the Active Work Item Accurate
- `.claude/rules/memory-review-and-save.md`: Review and Save Project Memory
- `.claude/rules/plain-english-artifacts.md`: Write Artifacts in Plain English
- `.claude/rules/session-handoff.md`: Prepare a Session Handoff
- `.claude/rules/shared-repository-work.md`: Work Safely in a Shared Repository
- `.claude/rules/work-item-folders.md`: Local Work-Item Folders

Path-scoped. Claude Code loads each one when it reads a matching file. Codex: open the rule before working on a matching path.

| Paths | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-external-knowledge/**` | `.claude/rules/ai-external-knowledge.md` |
| `requirements/**`, `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`, `PROJECT.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `system-guide/**`, `ai-external-knowledge/**`, `**/README.md` | `.claude/rules/publish-project-documents.md` |
<!-- toolkit:rules:end -->

## Project map

| Path | What is there, and when to open it |
| --- | --- |
| `PROJECT.md` | Purpose, scope, owners, systems, and tracker; open for project context. |
| `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md` | Phases (`P01`) and work units, each naming its work item ID; open for sequencing. |
| `DECISIONS.md` | Decisions for the whole project; open before changing direction. |
| `requirements/` | Delivered functional behavior by area; read its `AGENTS.md` before editing. |
| `system-guide/` | Guide to the current system, one file per area; open for questions about existing structure, purpose, connections, or impact. |
| `ai-external-knowledge/` | Captured outside sources by topic; `INDEX.md` lists them. Open when needed. |
| `tests/` | Test plans (`TEST-PLAN-TEMPLATE.md`) and checks; open before changing behavior. |
| `.toolkit.json` | Setup choices: tracker, memory system, Salesforce. Written by toolkit init; change it with `toolkit config set`. |
| `.work-items/` | Work items; each item's `DESIGN.md` sits beside its `WORK-ITEM.md`. `work-item-template/` is the form. `DASHBOARD.md` there is a generated status board. |
| `.memory/` | Current focus, index, glossary, and linked topic notes; open the folder as an Obsidian vault if wanted. Read its `AGENTS.md` before editing. |

## Commands

| Need | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Check the toolkit setup, tracker, and memory | `toolkit doctor`; the `project-setup` skill fixes what it reports. |
| Build, test, or deploy | `<Verified project commands and target environment; do not infer from this template.>` |

## How to write replies

Claude Code applies the Plain English output style to chat. Codex and helper agents follow these lines instead.

- Start with the answer, result, or current status. Answer what was asked. Keep it short; add detail when asked.
- Use ordinary words. Explain an unfamiliar term the first time it matters. Use the exact name a system uses, the same way every time.
- Write literally: no metaphors, idioms, jokes, or picture words in place of the real name. State the point directly, without a "not this, but that" setup.
- Use paragraphs for a connected explanation, bullets for separate items or choices, and a heading only when it names what is under it.
- When asking for a decision, name the choice and the difference that matters, and recommend one.
- Use the exact status word: written, built, tested, merged, installed, or seen working. Say something works only when you saw it work.
- Leave out routine narration of process and helper activity. Give one direct line when the owner lost something, an action cannot be undone, work waits on the owner, or there is a cost.
